newsitem.title: USA: NTSB puts airline fuel-tank steps on urgent list.
newsitem.headline: NTSB puts airline fuel-tank steps on urgent list.

text.p: The National Transportation Safety Board Tuesday added to its "most wanted" list of safety recommendations certain steps regulators could take to prevent explosions in airline fuel tanks.

The recommendations stem from last summer's explosion of TWA flight 800 off the coast of New York. To be on the annual "most wanted" list, a recommendation must have a national impact on transportation safety, concern a highly visible safety issue, or be of great public interest.
The NTSB also puts weight on recommendations that regulators do not act on for an "inordinately" long period.
The safety agency wants the Federal Aviation Administration to require airlines to reduce the likelihood that explosive mixtures can occur in airplane fuel tanks.

The agency, in particular, urged the FAA to look at requiring airlines to refuel the centre wing tank from cooler ground-fuel tanks. The NTSB also suggested close monitoring and management of fuel temperatures in the centre tank.
NTSB officials complained that the FAA has sought advice, rather than taken action, in response to initial NTSB fuel-tank recommendations made at the end of 1996.
Other recommendations on the "most wanted" dealt with:
-- Installation of smoke detectors and fire suppressors in all passenger-airline cargo holds. The recommendation stems from last May's ValuJet Inc. crash.
-- Use of automatic recording devices -- much like airline flight-data recorders -- in all modes of transporation, including ships, trucks and rail rapid transit.
-- Research into on-board ice-detection systems for aircraft as well as revised airline icing citeria.
